findings.claim: The one-glance verdict never resolves: status.attention stayed "unknown" for the entire observation window (~4 min) because node "judge" has no declared budget (silenceUnevaluated: [{node: judge, reason: no_declared_budget}]). Meanwhile judge has been in "running" with no event since 2026-08-18T21:30:34.721Z and headSequence never advanced past 13 content events. The operator asking "can I go back to sleep?" gets neither yes nor no, and the answer is structurally incapable of changing while the run is stuck — exactly the case where they must NOT sleep.
findings.remediation: Make a missing budget itself an attention-raising condition, not an evaluation opt-out. Apply a default silence budget (or an execution-level fallback) so any node silent past it flips attention to needs-attention with kind "silence_exceeded"; reserve "unknown" for the first moments after start, and never let "unknown" persist unbounded on a running node.

findings.claim: A real failure is invisible at a glance. Event seq 11 records flaky_check outcome "retryable_failure", reason "tool_exited_non_zero", with evidence refs, and the node dropped back to queued. status reports failed: 0, queued: 1, untriagedInterruptions: [], and no attentionReason for flaky_check. The retrying/flapping node is indistinguishable from a node that is normally waiting; only a full event-tail read (a second, non-glance step) reveals it.
findings.remediation: Surface failure history in the status summary: add counters/fields such as retryingNodes, recentFailures (node, reason, count, lastAt), and include a retry-after-failure node in attentionReasons. A node that has failed and not yet re-succeeded should not be summarized under the same bucket as a fresh queued node.

findings.claim: There is no wake path for a stall. wake_arm/wake_wait ring only on content appends past the cursor; two consecutive blocking waits (60s then 120s) both returned outcome "timeout" while the execution was frozen mid-run. Sleeping is therefore only safe when the graph is making progress — the silent-hang case, the one the operator most needs to be woken for, produces no ring by construction.
findings.remediation: Add a deadline/liveness ring: let wake_arm accept an attention-change or silence-deadline trigger (e.g. armOn: "attention_change" | "silence_exceeded", or a maxSilenceSeconds) so the lease rings when the log STOPS moving as well as when it moves. Distinguish the timeout reply from a "still healthy, nothing due" reply so the operator can tell an idle wait from a stalled run.

findings.claim: status ships absolute timestamps only (lastEventAt, nodeLastEventAt, startedAt) and no elapsed/age or expected-duration fields. To notice that judge has been silent for minutes the operator must fetch wall-clock time and subtract per node — arithmetic, not a glance. Nothing in the payload states "judge silent 4m".
findings.remediation: Include derived staleness in the status payload: perNode silenceSeconds, executionSilenceSeconds, and (where a budget exists) budgetRemainingSeconds, so staleness is readable without external clock math.

findings.claim: attentionReasons state a cause but no operator action. "no_declared_budget" on node judge tells the operator why the monitor is mute; it does not tell them whether to wait, inspect, or intervene, and the MCP surface exposes no way to declare a budget on a live execution to resolve the unknown.
findings.remediation: Attach a suggested action and a resolving affordance to each attention reason (e.g. nextAction: "declare budget or inspect node" plus a tool that sets/overrides a node's silence budget on a running execution), so an "unknown" is actionable rather than terminal.

findings.claim: The glance view omits the operator's own liveness posture. status does not indicate whether any wake lease is armed; wake_status is a separate call and returned live: false before arming. An operator can read a benign-looking status, sleep, and be unaware that nothing is watching on their behalf.
findings.remediation: Include a compact lease summary in status (armed: bool, cursor, lastConsumed) so "is anything set to wake me?" is answered by the same single call as "is anything wrong?".
